papers.title_in_file: SegNet: A Deep Convolutional Encoder-Decoder Architecture for Image Segmentation
papers.version_note: arXiv:1511.00561v3 (10 Oct 2016), the IEEE TPAMI-style version; the file name says 2015-11 but the text is the v3 revision.

figures.shows: Two rows of five photographs each (road scenes above, indoor scenes below), each followed by a colour-coded segmentation map predicted by SegNet; no axes; the colour legend is not printed.
figures.confirmed_by: Some example test results produced on randomly sampled road scene images from Google and indoor test scenes from the SUN RGB-D dataset

figures.shows: SegNet architecture: an RGB input image passes through a column chain of Conv+Batch Normalisation+ReLU blocks (blue) and Pooling blocks (green) in the encoder, then Upsampling (red) and Conv blocks in the decoder, then a Softmax layer (yellow) to the output segmentation; arrows labelled Pooling Indices run from each encoder pooling layer to the matching decoder upsampling layer; no fully connected layers.
figures.confirmed_by: The encoder network consists of 13 convolutional layers which correspond to the ﬁrst 13 convolutional layers in the VGG16 network

figures.shows: Left (SegNet): a 2 x 2 map of values a, b, c, d is upsampled using max-pooling indices into a 4 x 4 sparse map with zeros, then convolved with trainable decoder filters. Right (FCN): a 2 x 2 map is deconvolved for upsampling to a 4 x 4 map x1 to x16 and added element-wise to a dimensionality-reduced encoder feature map y1 to y16.
figures.confirmed_by: On the left in Fig. 3 is the decoding technique used by SegNet (also SegNet-Basic), where there is no learning involved in the upsampling step.

figures.shows: Eight decoder variants (rows: Bilinear-Interpolation, SegNet-Basic, SegNet-Basic-EncoderAddition, SegNet-Basic-SingleChannelDecoder, FCN-Basic, FCN-Basic-NoAddition, FCN-Basic-NoDimReduction, FCN-Basic-NoAddition-NoDimReduction); columns params (M), storage multiplier, inference time (ms), and G, C, mIoU, BF for test and G, C, mIoU for train under median frequency balancing, and the same under natural frequency balancing. Best values in bold.
figures.confirmed_by: In Table 1 we report the numerical results of our analysis.

figures.shows: Five CamVid day and dusk test images in columns; rows are the test sample, ground truth, SegNet, DeepLab-LargeFOV, DeepLab-LargeFOV-denseCRF, FCN, FCN (learn deconv) and DeconvNet, each a colour-coded segmentation map. No axes or numeric values.
figures.confirmed_by: The qualitative comparisons of SegNet predictions with other deep architectures can be seen in Fig. 4.

figures.shows: Per-class accuracy (Building, Tree, Sky, Car, Sign-Symbol, Road, Pedestrian, Fence, Column-Pole, Side-walk, Bicyclist), class average, global average, mIoU and BF for non-deep methods, SegNet trained on the 3.5K dataset for 140K iterations, and CRF based approaches on CamVid.
figures.confirmed_by: The results in Table 2 show SegNet-Basic, SegNet obtain competitive results when compared with methods which use CRFs.

figures.shows: CamVid test metrics G, C, mIoU, BF at 40K, 80K and more than 80K iterations plus the maximum iteration count, for SegNet, DeepLab-LargeFOV, DeepLab-LargeFOV-denseCRF, FCN, FCN (learnt deconv) and DeconvNet trained without class balancing on 3433 road scenes.
figures.confirmed_by: In Table 3 we compare SegNet’s performance with now widely adopted fully convolutional architectures for segmentation.

figures.shows: SUN RGB-D test metrics G, C, mIoU, BF at 80K, 140K and more than 140K iterations plus the maximum iteration count, for SegNet, DeepLab-LargeFOV, DeepLab-LargeFOV-denseCRF, FCN (learnt deconv) and DeconvNet, trained on indoor scenes with RGB only.
figures.confirmed_by: The quantitative results in Table 4 show that all the deep architectures share low mIoU and boundary metrics.

figures.shows: Five SUN RGB-D indoor test images in columns; rows are the test sample, ground truth, SegNet, DeepLab-LargeFOV, DeepLab-LargeFOV-denseCRF, FCN (learnt deconv) and DeconvNet, each a colour-coded segmentation map; black marks regions without ground truth labels. No axes or numeric values.
figures.confirmed_by: The qualitative results of SegNet on samples of indoor scenes of different types such as bedroom, living room, laboratory, meeting room, bathroom are shown in Fig. 5.

figures.shows: Class accuracy of SegNet on each of the 37 SUN RGB-D classes, from Wall (83.42) and Floor (93.43) down to Shower curtain (0.03) and Floor mat (0.00).
figures.confirmed_by: The accuracies reported in Table 5 clearly show that larger classes have reasonable accuracy and smaller classes have lower accuracies.

figures.shows: For SegNet, DeepLab-LargeFOV, FCN (learnt deconv) and DeconvNet: forward pass (ms), backward pass (ms), GPU training memory (MB), GPU inference memory (MB) and model size (MB). DeepLab-LargeFOV has the lowest times and training memory; SegNet has the lowest inference memory (1052 MB).
figures.confirmed_by: This can be seen from the compute statistics in Table 6.

papers.what_it_is: SegNet, a convolutional encoder-decoder network for pixel-wise semantic segmentation whose decoder upsamples with the encoder's max-pooling indices, analysed against FCN variants and benchmarked on CamVid road scenes and SUN RGB-D indoor scenes.

assertions.value: The authors state that the SegNet encoder network is topologically identical to the 13 convolutional layers of the VGG16 network.
quotes: The architecture of the encoder network is topologically identical to the 13 convolutional layers in the VGG16 network [1].
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that discarding the fully connected layers reduces the SegNet encoder parameters from 134M to 14.7M.
quotes: This also reduces the number of parameters in the SegNet encoder network signiﬁcantly (from 134M to 14.7M)
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that each encoder layer has a corresponding decoder layer, so the decoder network has 13 layers.
quotes: Each encoder layer has a corresponding decoder layer and hence the decoder network has 13 layers.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the decoder uses the pooling indices computed in the max-pooling step of the corresponding encoder to perform non-linear upsampling.
quotes: Speciﬁcally, the decoder uses pooling indices computed in the max-pooling step of the corresponding encoder to perform non-linear upsampling.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract defines the SegNet decoder technique.

assertions.value: The authors state that using the pooling indices eliminates the need for learning to upsample.
quotes: This eliminates the need for learning to upsample.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that the upsampled maps are sparse and are then convolved with trainable filters to produce dense feature maps.
quotes: The upsampled maps are sparse and are then convolved with trainable ﬁlters to produce dense feature maps.
assertions.certainty_reason: The abstract defines the decoder step.

assertions.value: The authors state that each encoder convolves with a filter bank, applies batch normalization and ReLU, then max-pooling with a 2 x 2 window and stride 2 and sub-sampling by a factor of 2.
quotes: Following that, max-pooling with a 2 × 2 window and stride 2 (non-overlapping window) is performed and the resulting output is sub-sampled by a factor of 2.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its encoder block.

assertions.value: The authors state that storing only the max-pooling indices can in principle be done using 2 bits for each 2 x 2 pooling window.
quotes: In principle, this can be done using 2 bits for each 2 × 2 pooling window and is thus much more efﬁcient to store as compared to memorizing feature map(s) in ﬂoat precision.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines what it stores.

assertions.value: The authors state that this lower memory storage results in a slight loss of accuracy but is still suitable for practical applications.
quotes: this lower memory storage results in a slight loss of accuracy but is still suitable for practical applications.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that the decoder upsamples its input using the memorized max-pooling indices, which produces sparse feature maps.
quotes: The appropriate decoder in the decoder network upsamples its input feature map(s) using the memorized max-pooling indices from the corresponding encoder feature map(s). This step produces sparse feature map(s).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its decoder step.

assertions.value: The authors state that the output of the soft-max classifier is a K channel image of probabilities, where K is the number of classes, and each pixel is classified independently.
quotes: The output of the soft-max classiﬁer is a K channel image of probabilities where K is the number of classes.
This soft-max classiﬁes each pixel independently.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its output layer.

assertions.value: The authors state that U-Net does not reuse pooling indices but transfers the entire feature map to the corresponding decoders, at the cost of more memory.
quotes: does not reuse pooling indices but instead transfers the entire feature map (at the cost of more memory) to the corresponding decoders
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that DeconvNet has a much larger parameterization, needs more computational resources and is harder to train end-to-end, primarily due to its fully connected layers.
quotes: DeconvNet has a much larger parameterization, needs more computational resources and is harder to train end-to-end (Table 6), primarily due to the use of fully connected layers
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors list three practical advantages of reusing max-pooling indices in decoding: it improves boundary delineation, it reduces the number of parameters enabling end-to-end training, and the form of upsampling can be incorporated into any encoder-decoder architecture.
quotes: Reusing max-pooling indices in the decoding process has several practical

advantages; (i) it improves boundary delineation , (ii) it reduces the number of parameters enabling end-to-end training, and (iii) this form of upsampling can be incorporated into any encoder-decoder architecture
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that if memory during inference is not constrained, all the encoder feature maps can be stored, but this is usually not the case in practical applications.
quotes: If memory during inference is not constrained, then all the encoder feature maps (after subsampling) can be stored. This is usually not the case in practical applications
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors define SegNet-Basic as a smaller version of SegNet with 4 encoders and 4 decoders, used to analyse decoder variants.
quotes: we use a smaller version of SegNet, termed SegNet-Basic 1, which has 4 encoders and 4 decoders.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines SegNet-Basic.

assertions.value: The authors state that SegNet-Basic uses a constant kernel size of 7 x 7 over all encoder and decoder layers, so a pixel in the layer 4 feature map traces back to a 106 x 106 pixel context window in the input image.
quotes: a constant kernel size of 7 × 7 over all the encoder and decoder layers is chosen to provide a wide context for smooth labelling i.e. a pixel in the deepest layer feature map (layer 4) can be traced back to a context window in the input image of 106×106 pixels.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that SegNet-Basic uses batch normalization after each convolutional layer, no biases after convolutions and no ReLU nonlinearity in the decoder network.
quotes: Batch normalization is used after each convolutional layer in both the encoder and decoder network. No biases are used after convolutions and no ReLU nonlinearity is present in the decoder network.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors define FCN-Basic as a comparable version of FCN that shares the same encoder network as SegNet-Basic but uses the FCN decoding technique in all its decoders.
quotes: shares the same encoder network as SegNet-Basic but with the FCN decoding technique (see Fig. 3) used in all its decoders.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines FCN-Basic.

assertions.value: The authors state that the FCN decoder reduces the encoder feature maps of 64 channels by convolving with 1 x 1 x 64 x K trainable filters, where K is the number of classes, and sets the upsampling kernel size to 8 x 8.
quotes: Dimensionality reduction of the encoder feature maps, say of 64 channels, is performed by convolving them with 1 × 1 × 64 × K trainable ﬁlters, where K is the number of classes.
We set the kernel size to 8 × 8.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the FCN decoder it compares against.

assertions.value: The authors define SegNet-Basic-SingleChannelDecoder as a variant whose decoder filters are single channel, which they state reduces the number of trainable parameters and inference time significantly.
quotes: This variant (SegNetBasic-SingleChannelDecoder) reduces the number of trainable parameters and inference time signiﬁcantly.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines this variant.

assertions.value: The authors define FCN-Basic-NoAddition as an FCN-Basic variant that discards the encoder feature map addition step and only learns the upsampling kernels.
quotes: We can also create a variant of the FCN-Basic model which discards the encoder feature map addition step and only learns the upsampling kernels (FCN-Basic-NoAddition).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines this variant.

assertions.value: The authors define a Bilinear-Interpolation variant that upsamples using fixed bilinear interpolation weights and therefore requires no learning for upsampling.
quotes: we study upsampling using ﬁxed bilinear interpolation weights which therefore requires no learning for upsampling (Bilinear-Interpolation).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines this variant.

assertions.value: The authors define SegNet-BasicEncoderAddition as a more memory intensive variant that adds 64 encoder feature maps at each layer to the output feature maps of the SegNet decoder.
quotes: we can add 64 encoder feature maps at each layer to the corresponding output feature maps from the SegNet decoder to create a more memory intensive variant of SegNet (SegNet-BasicEncoderAddition).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines this variant.

assertions.value: The authors define FCN-Basic-NoDimReduction as a more memory intensive FCN-Basic variant in which the final encoder feature map is not compressed to K channels, so the number of channels at the end of each decoder equals that of the corresponding encoder, 64.
quotes: Another and more memory intensive FCN-Basic variant (FCN-Basic-NoDimReduction) is where there is no dimensionality reduction performed for the encoder feature maps.
Therefore, the number of channels at the end of each decoder is the same as the corresponding encoder (i.e 64).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines this variant.

assertions.value: The authors report that storing 64 feature maps of the first layer of FCN-Basic at 180 x 240 resolution in 32 bit floating point precision takes 11MB, and that dimensionality reduction to 11 feature maps requires approximately 1.9MB.
quotes: storing 64 feature maps of the ﬁrst layer of FCN-Basic at 180 × 240 resolution in 32 bit ﬂoating point precision takes 11MB.
This can be made smaller using dimensionality reduction to the 11 feature maps which requires ≈ 1.9MB storage.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own storage accounting for the FCN decoder (a computed figure, not an experiment).

assertions.value: The authors report that SegNet requires almost negligible storage cost for the pooling indices, .17MB if stored using 2 bits per 2 x 2 pooling window.
quotes: SegNet on the other hand requires almost negligible storage cost for the pooling indices (.17MB if stored using 2 bits per 2 × 2 pooling window).
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own storage accounting (a computed figure, not an experiment).

assertions.value: The authors report that other generic variants, upsampling feature maps by replication or by using a fixed sparse array of indices, performed quite poorly in comparison to the variants above.
quotes: We also tried other generic variants where feature maps are simply upsampled by replication [7], or by using a ﬁxed (and
sparse) array of indices for upsampling. These performed quite poorly in comparison to the above variants.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no numbers for these variants.

assertions.value: The authors report that a variant without max-pooling and sub-sampling in the encoder network consumes more memory, takes longer to converge and performs poorly.
quotes: A variant without max-pooling and sub-sampling in the encoder network (decoders are redundant) consumes more memory, takes longer to converge and performs poorly.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors state that they release the Caffe implementation of all the variants to encourage reproduction of their results.
quotes: Finally, please note that to encourage reproduction of our results we release the Caffe implementation of all the variants
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the CamVid dataset used for the decoder variants has 367 training and 233 testing RGB images (day and dusk scenes) at 360 x 480 resolution and 11 classes.
quotes: This dataset is small, consisting of 367 training and 233 testing RGB images (day and dusk scenes) at 360 × 480 resolution.
The challenge is to segment 11 classes such as road, building, cars, pedestrians, signs, poles, side-walk etc.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that all decoder variants are trained with stochastic gradient descent with a fixed learning rate of 0.1 and momentum of 0.9, with mini-batches of 12 images, each image used only once in an epoch.
quotes: To train all the variants we use stochastic gradient descent (SGD) with a ﬁxed learning rate of 0.1 and momentum of 0.9
each mini-batch (12 images) is then picked in order thus ensuring that each image is used only once in an epoch.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that they train the variants until the training loss converges and select the model that performs highest on a validation dataset.
quotes: We select the model which performs highest on a validation dataset.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors define median frequency balancing as weighting each class in the loss by the ratio of the median of class frequencies computed on the entire training set divided by the class frequency.
quotes: where the weight assigned to a class in the loss function is the ratio of the median of class frequencies computed on the entire training set divided by the class frequency.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the weighting it uses.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use the cross-entropy loss as the training objective, summed over all the pixels in a mini-batch.
quotes: The loss is summed up over all the pixels in a mini-batch.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors define global accuracy (G) as the percentage of pixels correctly classified in the dataset, class average accuracy (C) as the mean of the predictive accuracy over all classes, and mean intersection over union (mIoU) over all classes as used in the Pascal VOC12 challenge.
quotes: global accuracy (G) which measures the percentage of pixels

correctly classiﬁed in the dataset, class average accuracy (C) is the mean of the predictive accuracy over all classes and mean intersection over union (mIoU) over all classes as used in the Pascal VOC12 challenge
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its metrics.

assertions.value: The authors state that the mIoU metric is more stringent than class average accuracy since it penalizes false positive predictions.
quotes: The mIoU metric is a more stringent metric than class average accuracy since it penalizes false positive predictions.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors report that Csurka et al. note that the mIoU metric does not always correspond to human qualitative judgements (ranks) of good quality segmentation.
quotes: note that this metric does not always correspond to human qualitative judgements (ranks) of good quality segmentation.
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the paper attributes to other work.

assertions.value: The authors define the boundary F1-measure (BF) as the F1-measure between predicted and ground truth class boundaries given a pixel tolerance distance, averaged per class into an image F1-measure and then over the test set.
quotes: The F1measure for each class that is present in the ground truth test image is averaged to produce an image F1-measure.
Then we compute the whole test set average, denoted the boundary F1-measure (BF) by average the image F1 measures.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its boundary metric.

assertions.value: The authors state that they used a value of 0.75% of the image diagonal as the tolerance distance for the boundary F1-measure.
quotes: We used a value of 0.75% of the image diagonal as the tolerance distance.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that they test each variant after each 1000 iterations on the CamVid validation set, which with a mini-batch size of 12 is approximately every 33 epochs.
quotes: We test each architectural variant after each 1000 iterations of optimization on the CamVid validation set until the training loss converges.
With a training mini-batch size of 12 this corresponds to testing approximately every 33 epochs (passes) through the training set.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that they select the iteration with the highest global accuracy on the validation set and report the three measures at this point on the held-out CamVid test set.
quotes: We select the iteration wherein the global accuracy is highest amongst the evaluations on the validation set. We report all the three measures of performance at this point on the held-out CamVid test set.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that they observed that reporting performance when class average is highest can often correspond to low global accuracy, indicating a perceptually noisy segmentation output.
quotes: We also observed that reporting the numerical performance when class average is highest can often correspond to low global accuracy indicating a perceptually noisy segmentation output.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that the average time for one forward pass was measured with their Caffe implementation, averaged over 50 measurements using a 360 x 480 input on an NVIDIA Titan GPU with cuDNN v3 acceleration.
quotes: We show the average time for one forward pass with our Caffe implementation, averaged over 50 measurements using a 360 × 480 input on an NVIDIA Titan GPU with cuDNN v3 acceleration.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states its own setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the upsampling layers in the SegNet variants are not optimised using cuDNN acceleration.
quotes: We note that the upsampling layers in the SegNet variants are not optimised using cuDNN acceleration.
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper states a limit on its own timing measurement.

assertions.value: Table 1 reports, for SegNet-Basic trained with median frequency balancing, an inference time of 52.6 ms and test global accuracy 82.7, class average 62.0, mIoU 47.7 and BF 35.78.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: Row and column assignment read from the rendered table on p.6 and checked against the figure.

assertions.value: Table 1 reports, for FCN-Basic trained with median frequency balancing, an inference time of 24.2 ms and test global accuracy 81.7, class average 62.4, mIoU 47.3 and BF 38.11.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: Row and column assignment read from the rendered table on p.6 and checked against the figure.

assertions.value: The authors report that bilinear interpolation based upsampling without any learning performs the worst based on all the measures of accuracy.
quotes: upsampling without any learning performs the worst based on all the measures of accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that the methods that use learning for upsampling (FCN-Basic and variants) or learn decoder filters after upsampling (SegNet-Basic and its variants) perform significantly better than bilinear interpolation.
quotes: All the other methods which either use learning for upsampling (FCN-Basic and variants) or learning decoder ﬁlters after upsampling (SegNet-Basic and its variants) perform signiﬁcantly better.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: The text does not give a significance test.

assertions.value: The authors report that SegNet-Basic and FCN-Basic perform equally well on this test over all the measures of accuracy.
quotes: When we compare SegNet-Basic and FCN-Basic we see that both perform equally well on this test over all the measures of accuracy.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that SegNet uses less memory during inference since it only stores max-pooling indices, while FCN-Basic stores encoder feature maps in full, which consumes much more memory (11 times more).
quotes: The difference is that SegNet uses less memory during inference since it only stores max-pooling indices. On the other hand FCN-Basic stores encoder feature maps in full which consumes much more memory (11 times more).
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that FCN-Basic, which has 11 feature maps in each decoder layer against 64 in SegNet-Basic, is faster during inference.
quotes: SegNet-Basic has a decoder with 64 feature maps in each decoder layer. In comparison FCN-Basic, which uses dimensionality reduction, has fewer (11) feature maps in each decoder layer.
hence FCN-Basic is faster during inference (forward pass).
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that SegNet-Basic achieves higher training accuracy than FCN-Basic for the same number of iterations.
quotes: This endows it with more ﬂexibility and hence achieves higher training accuracy than FCN-Basic for the same number of iterations.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that SegNet-Basic has an advantage over FCN-Basic when inference time memory is constrained but inference time can be compromised to some extent.
quotes: Overall we see that SegNet-Basic has an advantage over FCN-Basic when inference time memory is constrained but where inference time can be compromised to some extent.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors report that the accuracy of FCN-Basic-NoAddition is lower than that of FCN-Basic, with a large drop in the BF measure, and conclude that it is vital to capture the information present in the encoder feature maps.
quotes: The accuracy of FCN-Basic-NoAddition is also lower as compared to FCN-Basic.
In particular, note the large drop in the BF measure between these two variants.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that the performance of SegNet-Basic is superior to FCN-Basic-NoAddition, which they attribute in part to its larger decoder size.
quotes: The performance of SegNet-Basic is superior, in part due to its larger decoder size.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that FCN-Basic-NoAddition-NoDimReduction performs poorer than SegNet-Basic on the test and that its training accuracy is lower for the same number of training epochs.
quotes: The performance of this FCN variant is poorer than SegNet-Basic in test but also its training accuracy is lower for the same number of training epochs.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that comparing FCN-Basic-NoAddition with SegNet-Basic-SingleChannelDecoder shows that using max-pooling indices for upsampling and an overall larger decoder leads to better performance.
quotes: Another interesting comparison between FCN-BasicNoAddition and SegNet-Basic-SingleChannelDecoder shows that using max-pooling indices for upsampling and an overall larger decoder leads to better performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that when neither memory nor inference time is constrained, larger models such as FCN-Basic-NoDimReduction and SegNet-EncoderAddition are more accurate than the other variants.
quotes: In the best case, when both memory and inference time is not constrained, larger models such as FCN-Basic-NoDimReduction and SegNet-EncoderAddition are
both more accurate than the other variants.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that discarding dimensionality reduction in the FCN-Basic model leads to the best performance amongst the FCN-Basic variants, with a high BF score.
quotes: discarding dimensionality reduction in the FCN-Basic model leads to the best performance amongst the FCN-Basic variants with a high BF score.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that without class balancing (natural frequency) the results are poorer for all the variants, particularly for class average accuracy and the mIoU metric.
quotes: Here, we can observe that without weighting the results are poorer for all the variants, particularly for class average accuracy and mIoU metric.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that the global accuracy is the highest without weighting, since the majority of the scene is dominated by sky, road and building pixels.
quotes: The global accuracy is the highest without weighting since the majority of the scene is dominated by sky, road and building pixels.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors report that apart from this, all the inferences from the comparative analysis of variants hold for natural frequency balancing too, including the trends for the BF measure.
quotes: Apart from this all the inference from the comparative analysis of variants holds true for natural frequency balancing too, including the trends for the BF measure.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.

assertions.value: The authors conclude from the decoder analysis that the best performance is achieved when encoder feature maps are stored in full, reflected most clearly in the semantic contour delineation metric (BF).
quotes: The best performance is achieved when encoder feature maps are stored in full. This is reﬂected in the semantic contour delineation metric (BF) most clearly.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that when memory during inference is constrained, compressed forms of encoder feature maps (dimensionality reduction, max-pooling indices) can be stored and used with an appropriate decoder (for example SegNet type) to improve performance.
quotes: When memory during inference is constrained, then compressed forms of encoder feature maps (dimensionality reduction, max-pooling indices) can be stored and used with an appropriate decoder (e.g. SegNet type) to improve performance.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that the quantitative assessments show that SegNet provides good performance with competitive inference time and is the most efficient inference memory-wise as compared to other architectures.
quotes: These quantitative assessments show that SegNet provides good performance with competitive inference time and most efﬁcient inference memory-wise as compared to other architectures.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: The authors state that SegNet is significantly smaller in the number of trainable parameters than other competing architectures and can be trained end-to-end using stochastic gradient descent.
quotes: It is also signiﬁcantly smaller in the number of trainable parameters than other competing architectures and can be trained end-to-end using stochastic gradient descent.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the paper gives no separate proof at this point.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 4: in the five CamVid test samples, the SegNet row shows thin vertical pole-like structures that the ground truth row also shows, and the DeepLab-LargeFOV rows show smoother regions with fewer thin structures.
quotes: SegNet shows superior performance, particularly with its ability to delineate boundaries, as
DeepLab-LargeFOV is the most efﬁcient model and with CRF post-processing can produce competitive results although smaller classes are lost.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: A visual reading of a 100 dpi page image; the paper gives no numeric score for these samples.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 5: SegNet predictions on the five SUN RGB-D test scenes show large uniform regions for bed, sofa and table scenes and visibly mixed small regions on the cluttered third scene, and the caption states that parts of an image without ground truth labels are shown in black.
quotes: Overall rhe segmentation quality is better when object classes are reasonably sized but is very noisy when the scene is more cluttered.
Note that often parts of an image of a scene do not have ground truth labels and these are shown in black colour.
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: A visual reading of a 100 dpi page image; the paper gives no numeric score for these samples.

assertions.value: Read from Figure 1: the figure shows five road scene images and five indoor scene images, each with a colour-coded segmentation below it, and the text states that the road scene images come from Google and the indoor scenes from the SUN RGB-D dataset.
quotes: Some example test results produced on randomly sampled road scene images from Google and indoor test scenes from the SUN RGB-D dataset
assertions.certainty_reason: Single-study result reported by the authors.
assertions.reader_inference: Qualitative figure only; the paper reports no metric for these images.
